The Last Lighthouse Keeper

On a rock off the Hebrides, the final keeper hands over the lamp.

The boat comes on Thursdays, weather permitting. Morag has learned not to count on it. She keeps a ledger of the days it did not come, and the ledger is longer than she likes to admit.

Automation arrived in 1998. The lamp turns by itself now, and a sensor reports fog to a station on the mainland. The keepers were pensioned off one by one.

What remains is the part no sensor reports: the smell of paraffin that never left the stairwell, the handwriting in the logbooks, the way the wind sounds in the gallery rail.
